items.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: I toured all through the south with Johnny Hodges

ctx.x: You know I want to ask you a question here. As we can kind of try to relate this to jazz, you say the music was expensive because it cost you something. And I was thinking there seems to be a spiritual aspect, even to the jazz, even, but a lot of preachers said, oh, that’s the devil’s music. But at the same time many of those were the backup musicians for the R&B groups.

Of course. John Coltrane was in my band. We went through the south. John Coltrane was in my band, he was in Paul “Hucklebuck” Williams, who had the big record “The Hucklebuck” before Chubby Checker got it and called it “The Twist.” John Coltrane was in that band. I toured all through the south with Johnny Hodges, Richard oh, God he was killed in the car with Clifford Brown —
